chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Backbiting is more rapid in consuming the religion of the Muslim man than food is in his belly.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Sitting in the mosque awaiting the prayer is worship as long as nothing occurs.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what occurs?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Backbiting.'
ai.seo_question: How does backbiting affect a Muslim's religion according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to emphasize that backbiting is a spiritual corrosive that consumes faith more rapidly than physical food, a metaphor highlighting its invisible yet destructive nature. The hadith further contextualizes the virtue of sitting in the mosque for prayer (intizar al-salah) by noting that it is invalidated if accompanied by backbiting, illustrating how a single major sin can nullify the reward of a righteous act.
